speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our Ministerial Statements will address Oral Question Nos 1 to 5 and 26 to 28 and Written Question Nos 28, 29 and 31 to 33 on today's Order Paper.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will cover questions on the KTV and Jurong Fishery Port clusters, our COVID-19 vaccination programme and our plans to transit to live normally with COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Murali Pillai1,2, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim3, Mr Darryl David4,5, Mr Xie Yao Quan6,7, Mr Yip Hon Weng8, Mr Seah Kian Peng9, Ms Raeesah Khan10 and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin11 have filed Oral and Written Questions scheduled for future Sittings on these issues.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As today’s Ministerial Statements would address those questions, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I would like to invite these Members to seek clarifications, should they have any, on these issues after the Ministerial Statements.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And should their queries be sufficiently addressed, it may not be necessary for them to proceed with their Parliamentary Questions (PQs) for future Sittings.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: On Monday, 12 July 2021, MOH detected several COVID-19 positive cases amongst individuals who frequented KTV bars and lounges.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These individuals included patrons of the bars and hostesses who worked in the lounges.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These activities were considered very high risk and had been disallowed since the beginning of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The cluster grew rapidly and MOH moved in quickly to isolate infected persons.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The pivoted nightlife establishments cannot resume operations until they pass inspections to ensure that safe management measure protocols are in place and they have received written approval.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked if we would consider making the individuals in the KTV cluster pay for their COVID-19 medical expenses in full.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are all upset by the irresponsible behaviour of the individuals involved in this KTV cluster, but we still have a public responsibility to ensure that everyone receives the medical care that they need.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We also do not want individuals, especially those who are infected, to avoid getting tested and treated, or hide where they have been from contact tracers, because they are afraid of getting penalised.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will make it harder to contain the spread and would cost us more in the long run.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We were on the path towards progressive opening and the KTV cluster was a major unexpected bump on the road.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hence, on 16 July, the MTF announced our decision to maintain our then current safe management posture.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We made some adjustments to the rules for eating in restaurants, we called it the "two-five rule".

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Two, if you are unvaccinated; five, you can dine together, provided everyone is fully vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Based on how the cluster has developed, we still believe that was the correct call.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For the past three days, the daily increase in infection for the cluster was six, five and five respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Unfortunately, things got derailed due to a larger and more troublesome cluster and this is the Jurong Fishery Port cluster.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: On the evening of Friday, 16 July 2021, we started to detect multiple infections at the Jurong Fishery Port, as well as in Hong Lim market.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This involved fishmongers, their assistants going about an honest living, collecting fishes at the fishery port, but unwittingly getting infected and then transmitting to more people in the markets and communities where they ply their trade.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOH, with the help of NEA, took immediate steps to prevent further spread by stopping the fishmongers and their assistants from setting up stalls on Sunday, 18 July 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It was very tough to tell them "You can't set up stalls".

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We then issued Health Risk Warnings which required them to undergo PCR tests and isolate themselves until they get a negative result.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The numbers are a bit different from what I reported earlier as we cleaned up the numbers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This indicated that significant community transmission had most likely already silently occurred in the days before 18 July 2021, Sunday.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Markets are frequented by wide segments of the public, particularly seniors, of whom one-quarter are still not fully vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The risk of infections rising uncontrollably could not be ruled out.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This came into effect on 22 July 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We did this to buy ourselves time, precious time, to get more of our population vaccinated, so that we can continue on our path towards living with COVID-19 safely.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The preliminary phylogenetic findings suggest that while the KTV and Jurong Fishery Port clusters were all driven by the Delta variant, it is distinct from the Delta variant that infected Tan Tock Seng Hospital and the Changi Airport clusters.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The recent clusters have a Delta strain that is more closely related to what we detected in imported cases from our immediate region.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, there are also slight genetic differences between the strains in the two clusters, suggesting that there were multiple introduction points.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is still growing, but now at a slower rate.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The daily infection numbers over the last three days were 79, 79 and 46 respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Overall, we have seen a high number of daily cases at over 100 for the past several days.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But the situation is stabilising, with daily infections trending down.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Percentage of cases isolated or quarantined before turning COVID-19 positive is something we watch closely and it is on an upward trend which is good.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That means, when a person started to be detected as positive, he is already quarantined and isolated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: On 19 July, that was when the cluster first broke out, we had a total of 163 cases and only 27% were isolated before detection.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, we should have more than half of our cases already isolated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we can keep raising that percentage through tracing and testing, we can progressively suppress this wave of transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But our objective is not to stop transmissions completely.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is no longer possible, given how transmissible the Delta variant is and as we open up, people circulate more.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, the only possible way now to eradicate infections is to go into a hard circuit breaker for at least a month, probably two.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we do not want to be locked up.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Further, even if we do lock ourselves up, when the circuit breaker ends and we open up, cases will rise again.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We must instead find ways to live with this virus safely.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Several Members, namely Mr Yip Hon Weng, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, Ms Raeesah Khan, were interested to find out more about our transition plans to live with COVID-19 as an endemic disease.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Vaccinations are key to this transition and the national programme is progressing well.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By early September, it should be almost 80% having received two doses of mRNA vaccines.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This means that Singapore, by then, will have one of the highest vaccination rates in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It puts us in a strong position to transit to a COVID-19-resilient society.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our main worry is that our seniors, especially those 70 and above, are not sufficiently vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, just over 70% of them have received two doses of the vaccines.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked for an update on the home vaccination scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have launched nine home vaccination teams so far.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Further, more seniors are coming forward to our vaccination centres and also our mobile vaccination teams.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have been seeing about 500 seniors coming forward on a daily basis to receive their first doses for the past few weeks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But for the past few days, that number has doubled to over 1,000 every day now.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But it may be due to heightened awareness as a result of more community transmission, the lifting of rules that had previously deferred their vaccinations – for those with medical conditions – and also our very intensive outreach efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, our mobile teams have gone all the way to Pulau Ubin to vaccinate seniors who are living there.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We know of general practitioners (GPs) who persuaded and called up their clients, the seniors, persuaded them to go for vaccinations and then opened up their clinics for them to sit in the clinics the whole day so that they feel assured that if they feel unwell, help is always nearby, help from someone they trust, their GPs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are making such an extraordinary effort with our seniors because we are not prepared to accept the high fatality rates amongst the elderly that other countries had or are still experiencing.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Within a month or so, they should all have received their second doses and after that, another 14 days, they should all be strongly protected against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Even at our current rate of vaccination – 54% or so for two doses – the preliminary evidence is that it has been effective in reducing the incidence of severe illnesses and deaths.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The bottom line in orange is the number with severe illnesses requiring oxygen supplementation or ICU.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As Members can see, while daily infections had gone up sharply over the past couple of weeks, the number of patients with severe illnesses who required oxygen supplementation or are in ICU remained relatively low.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There was a slight uptick but relatively suppressed.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we are watching this closely because there is a time lag of one to two weeks between infection and the onset of severe illnesses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: While we are making good progress in vaccinating our people, we acknowledge that the recent reversion to Phase Two (Heightened Alert) has caused some confusion amongst members of the public.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They are asking: is the MTF still committed to the path towards normalcy and living with COVID-19?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For that is the only way for Singaporeans to regain our lives and livelihoods, for Singapore to reconnect with the world again, for our young to look into the future with hope.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Some countries, like the UK, have declared a Freedom Day recently, where all social restrictions are lifted all at once.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Others, like Israel and the Netherlands, opened up and saw sharp increases in infections and hospitalisations and had had to dial back very quickly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are not going to do a big bang because, predictably, things will then blow up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But even as we do so, we must bear in mind that until we reach a sufficiently high vaccination rate, especially amongst our seniors, we will continue to be vulnerable to unexpected setbacks – just like what we are going through now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: A high rate of vaccination will provide us with a more solid and stable base as we proceed on this journey.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The higher the vaccination rate, the more solid the ground we walk on.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, in a way, this is the most peculiar period of our transition, where we are clear about our mission, our will is firm, we have a broad plan but we do not have enough antibodies in all of us to ensure that we can follow through our plans without a hitch.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But let us not underestimate the progress we have made.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The roadmap is, in fact, being implemented as we speak.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Our attention often is on the Safe Management Measures, or SMMs, such as whether we can eat in restaurants.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But there at least three other important aspects, namely: (a) restoring economic and social activities, including connecting with the outside world; (b) remodelling COVID-19 healthcare protocols; and (c) shifting our collective psychology, which, I feel, is probably the hardest.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Minister Gan Kim Yong will speak about restoring economic activities while Minister Lawrence Wong will speak more about enabling more social activities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As we learn to live with COVID-19, our healthcare protocols must be remodelled.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If COVID-19 is, indeed, endemic, having 200 or more cases may not be an unusual thing at all.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: During an influenza season, our daily infection rates can go up to as high as 1,000 a day.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Imagine we treat influenza like we treat COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will put everyone suspected of influenza infections through polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests and then long isolated stays in hospitals.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Then, everyone they come into contact with will be quarantined.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This will disrupt the lives of many people.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Further, hospital beds will all be filled and many other patients who are sicker will be turned away.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The healthcare system will not be able to cope and that is clearly not the way to deal with an endemic disease.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, if we want to live with COVID-19 as an endemic disease, we cannot carry on with the current healthcare protocols.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They need to shift closer to how we treat influenza today – without extensive contact tracing and quarantine in dedicated facilities and hospitalising only those who are very ill.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But that can only happen when the likelihood of developing a very serious or life-threatening disease as a result of a COVID-19 infection has been significantly reduced by effective vaccination of our population, especially amongst the vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: With our current rate of vaccinations, we have started to take the first transition step to remodel our healthcare protocols.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As of last week, we had made the following changes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: First, greater use of community care facilities instead of hospitals.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Vaccinated individuals aged between 45 and 59 who test positive for COVID-19 and show no or mild symptoms can be directly admitted to community care facilities instead of going first to hospitals.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These community care facilities, currently, for example, are NTUC D'Resort as well as Civil Service Club (CSC) Loyang.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This was already the practice for all cases aged between 17 and 45, but we are now expanding the protocol to people up to 59 years old.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Meanwhile, we will plan for the next step.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will plan for the next one where perhaps 80% can be admitted to community care facilities and some can even start to recover at home.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Our tests have shown that the viral load in infected persons who are fully vaccinated falls very rapidly to a very low level after nine days.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are reviewing our policy to allow fully vaccinated patients to be discharged even earlier and to complete the rest of the isolation period at home if their home environment is suitable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The third change is the greater use of home quarantines.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These are amongst the first steps that we will take in the healthcare transition.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In the meantime, what we are experiencing in this current wave of transmission is also valuable because we are also witnessing a palpable shift in our collective psychology.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The first, I think, is a shift away from always focusing on infection numbers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We used to get a shock when we see high daily numbers because this will mean that a week or two from then, we will see more severe illnesses and deaths.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: However, in recent days, that mental link is starting to be broken as we know that, with vaccinations, high infection numbers need not necessarily mean more sickness and deaths.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Many people are now rightfully focusing on the number of people with severe illnesses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Many friends, including Members of this House, have been texting and asking me: why do we not publish the number of people with severe illnesses so that we know that vaccination works?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Actually, the media have been publishing these numbers every day for quite a while now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But our attention is always on the infection numbers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is good that the attention is now shifting.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I will not say that there is a huge psychological shift but I think the shift is starting to happen.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: A second shift is a greater acceptance of differentiated safe management measures between those who are vaccinated and those who are not.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There have been many calls to do this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan has also asked about this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is something which the MTF has always intended to do.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That was why we decided on the "two-five rule" for restaurants when the KTV cluster broke out.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But it was scuttled with our reversion to Phase Two (Heightened Alert).

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When our whole society is very highly vaccinated and we have transitioned to living with COVID-19, we should make very little differentiation between the vaccinated and the unvaccinated.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But during this period of transition, when we are still building up our resilience, differentiation by vaccination status is a practical way to open up some activities first while protecting those who are still vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The MTF will revisit this during our Phase Two (Heightened Alert) midpoint review and Minister Lawrence Wong will speak more about that later.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Murali Pillai will be comforted to know that MOH actively monitors international developments in medical treatment options for COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is done through the National Centre of Infectious Diseases (NCID) and an expert committee.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They have developed national treatment guidelines which are constantly updated based on new evidence.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They provide guidance to our doctors on the use of evidence-based medical treatment options for COVID-19 patients.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Our local institutions have also been participating actively in international multi-centre trials investigating novel COVID-19 therapeutics.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These trials have generated important data on new COVID-19 treatments such as remdesivir.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will continue to closely monitor developments in COVID-19 treatments, proactively procure therapeutic agents which are shown to be effective and maintain a stockpile based on projected needs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: To Mr Leon Perera’s question, factors that affect COVID-19 vaccine efficacy are an area of active study in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Persons who have contracted COVID-19 are clinically assessed for risk factors and scientific papers on the correlations may be published in future.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Antibody testing is not required after vaccination under Singapore’s National Vaccination Programme and we are actively reviewing the need for vaccine boosters.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Testing will remain very important, even as we transit to living with COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Because it is only through testing that we can know if we are infected and do the civic-minded thing in excusing ourselves from work and staying home.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we have to make testing simple, accessible and affordable, even more so than now, so that we can all do our part.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I believe many Members have done the breathalyser testing just now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it is one example of a test that is non-intrusive, simple, easy, accessible and fast.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Since mid-June, we have progressively rolled out regular Fast and Easy Tests for staff working in higher-risk settings.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This includes a network of 16 Quick Test Centres, which we intend to expand further.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In response to Ms Joan Pereira’s question, the Quick Test Centres will support small businesses by allowing their staff to walk in and get themselves tested and have their results recorded.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At some point, I believe, the Quick Test Centres should also be using breathalyser tests.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will continue to work with NEA to deploy wastewater testing across Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Currently, NEA has deployed 270 auto-samplers across about 200 sites.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Wastewater testing is an increasingly strategic resource as we learn to live with COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Where we place the sites is very important.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We can deploy them in areas where we suspect transmission is happening, such as around the markets that are currently affected, or where we know many unvaccinated seniors live.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Such testing is non-intrusive and would give us valuable early warning when COVID-19 starts to take hold in a locality; we will know very early.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And that will prompt us to take further public health measures in the affected residential estates.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Darryl David, Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Mr Murali Pillai asked about the safety of the COVID-19 vaccines.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: MOH has been publishing monthly safety data updates on our website.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It also gives an age breakdown of the affected persons and indeed, the majority are young people.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: While there is a small increased risk among those in the younger age groups relative to the baseline rate, the local incidence rate remains low.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: One of the reported cases is a full-time National Serviceman in the Singapore Armed Forces who is below 30 years old.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: None of the cases was from the Singapore Police Force and Singapore Civil Defence Force.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We implemented the Vaccine Injury Financial Assistance Programme or VIFAP to give greater peace of mind to people taking the vaccinations.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But remember that with or without vaccination, there is a baseline number of disease cases amongst our population.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Since the vast majority of Singaporeans have stepped forward to be vaccinated, there will naturally be numerous incidents which just happen to coincide with vaccinations.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Hence, we have to do what is practical and reasonable, which is to have VIFAP applications reviewed by a panel of medical experts, who will consider them against known evidence about the vaccines.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: A few Members have also asked about the Sinovac vaccine.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Sinovac vaccine is called CoronaVac but we always just call it Sinovac.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Sinovac is the company; the vaccine is CoronaVac but for simplicity, we just refer to it as the Sinovac vaccine.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Amongst them, 28% are Singapore Citizens and they are mostly young.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Of those who have taken the Sinovac vaccine, only 10% or in fact, less than 10% are Singaporean seniors above 60 years old.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The events comprise mainly allergic reactions such as itch and rashes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for concessions on safe management measures, the data on the efficacy of the Sinovac vaccine against the Delta variant is still building up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Sinovac has also recently submitted the required safety data for their application for the Pandemic Special Access Route approval to HSA.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: HSA and our Expert Committee are going through the various data.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When the evidence justifies it, we will certainly want to extend the concessions to individuals who have received the Sinovac or other vaccines which may qualify.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As a Government, we need to recognise that our society is diverse, with different segments of the population having different opinions, needs and wants.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When these differences cannot be reconciled, we agree to disagree, we live and let live.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the same time, we do our best to unite and forge a consensus, for what is a society without shared commonalities?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is what a responsible Government needs to do across a range of issues: from education, healthcare and public housing, to racial harmony and free trade.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We must always try to strike the right balance between forging a consensus as well as respecting diverse views.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is the same when it comes to learning to live with COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the one hand, we have the young, vaccinated individuals who feel that we should open up and allow vaccinated individuals to enjoy more social activities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the other hand, we still have a sizeable segment of older Singaporeans who for medical or other reasons are yet to be vaccinated and who remain vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Differentiated safe management measures is something we have to put in place for public health reasons and to protect the unvaccinated.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the same time, we must do our best to get more of the vulnerable vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As I reported just now, we are making progress.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for the non-vulnerable, as more of you get vaccinated, when you show more consideration to others, you are also doing your part to better protect the vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Remember, our children, our nieces or nephews, younger brothers and sisters under 12, will not be vaccinated for a while yet.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When we work together as a people, we will bring ourselves to a much stronger and more resilient position and our transition to living with COVID-19 will gather pace.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And we can look forward with confidence to living with an endemic COVID-19 because a high proportion of our population will be fully vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister Ong Ye Kung has given Members an update on the COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The virus is likely to become endemic eventually, like influenza, with the vast majority of us protected against the severe outcome of the virus, as long as we are fully vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are not there yet and we need to press on with vaccination, especially among the elderly.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As we journeyed towards this destination, we were never under the illusion that it would be straightforward and we expected to face a few bumps along the way.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The KTV and Jurong Fishery Port clusters are cases in point.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are determined to get to our destination of being a COVID-19-resilient Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But our journey must take into consideration public health realities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Sometimes, we may need to take a detour if we see hazards ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This way, we can ensure that we will get to our final destination safely, even though it may take a little longer.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The last one and a half years has been a very difficult ride for our businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is particularly so for sectors that are more affected by the tightening of Safe Management Measures, such as F&B, retail, sports and gyms and performance arts.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I know that the impact on them must be very severe.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister Wong and I met the F&B and Retailers' Trade Associations last week.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We appreciated their feedback, which helped MTI and MOF design the support packages for them as well as other affected businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the same time, I am heartened to see that many businesses have adapted their operations in response to the challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Food establishments and retail shops have leveraged online platforms and gyms have turned to virtual classes or moved some of their classes outdoors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Nevertheless, we know that these efforts are insufficient to fully compensate for the loss of income from their usual business model.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The aviation, tourism and MICE sectors have also been severely impacted due to travel restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, Singapore Airlines is now using some of its passenger planes to operate cargo flights to take advantage of the increase in cargo traffic, while operators in the tourism sector have come up with new and creative products to attract local visitors as foreign tourists have dried up.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Singapore Rediscover Vouchers would have helped them somewhat.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The construction, marine and process sectors are also under tremendous pressure.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They have had to make difficult but necessary worksite adjustments to protect workers' health and safety.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the same time, they have had to deal with labour shortages.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As a result, many have faced project cancellations and delays or shied away from taking on new projects.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We fully understand the challenges and uncertainties that our businesses and their workers are going through.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We ensured that firms that ran into cashflow problems could gain access to credit by enhancing our enterprise financing schemes and working with the banks to put in place a moratorium on loan repayment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Together, these efforts have helped avert massive business failures, a much deeper recession and higher unemployment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Businesses and workers have told us that while these support measures have been critical and helpful, they can only serve as temporary pain relief.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They would much prefer to resume their business fully and for the economy to grow again.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many are therefore transforming their businesses to seek out new opportunities and prepare for the recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I think this is the right attitude to have.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even as we manage the short-term impact of the pandemic, we should not lose sight of the future.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: COVID-19 has wreaked havoc on almost every single economy in the world, but those which can respond well and take the opportunity to adapt and transform quickly will emerge stronger and move ahead of others.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To ensure that we do not get left behind once the dust settles, we must turn this once-in-a-generation crisis into a once-in-a-generation opportunity, to transform our businesses, develop new areas of growth and strengthen our connections to the global economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We recognise that it is not easy for businesses to juggle everyday challenges during the pandemic and the need to change and transform for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is why we set up the Emerging Stronger Task force, or EST, at the height of the crisis in May last year, to look at how Singapore should refresh and re-imagine our economic strategies going forward.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The EST formed nine Alliances for Action, or AfAs, as a new model of public-private partnership to allow our businesses to move quickly and bounce back stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some of the AfAs have delivered promising results.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, the AfA on Safe and Innovative Visitor Experiences enabled us to testbed several ideas for safe MICE events, which provided some relief for the MICE sector while also elevating its international profile.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The AfA on Supply Chain Digitalisation saw the growing demand for supply chain transparency and resilience and created SGTraDex, which stands for Singapore Trade Data Exchange.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As a digital infrastructure, SGTraDex allows businesses to share data with each other in a trusted and safe manner, thereby allowing them to optimise their supply chain flows through Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: With more trades coming through Singapore, our position as a key node in the global supply chain is further strengthened.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For sectors that are doing well despite the pandemic, the Government's focus is to add wind to their sails, to help them create new products, forge new partnerships and break into new markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include the financial, ICT, biomedical manufacturing and electronics sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The AfA on medtech product development is another good example of our new partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Recognising the increasing prevalence of infectious and chronic diseases, it identified in-vitro diagnostics as a key sub-sector that we can grow.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will continue to work closely with industry and partner businesses in this endeavour to give them the support they need to raise their productivity, innovate and grow beyond our shores.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also help workers to be ready for the challenges in the new normal.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As businesses transform to remain competitive and seize new opportunities, workers will also need to learn new knowledge and acquire new skills.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The need for workers to upgrade and upskill is more urgent than ever.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Government is committed to walking this journey with our workers, every step of the way.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We introduced the SkillsFuture Movement in 2015 and intensified our efforts through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package since the pandemic started.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will work with MOM and the unions to encourage and support workers to tap on these schemes to stay relevant in their current jobs or retrain to enter new jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I also call on employers to continue working with the Government and the tripartite partners to upgrade and redesign jobs and invest in workforce training.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even as we plan ahead, we know that businesses are naturally concerned about what an endemic state means for their daily operations and the adjustments they may need to make as we get there.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some of the details are still being finalised and we will share them in future.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As our vaccination coverage increases, we will be in a much stronger position to ease our COVID-19 measures safely and confidently.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will begin to adjust our Safe Management Measures in stages, while keeping an eye on the number of serious cases.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Workplace restrictions will also be eased and progressively, more workers can go back to office.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Businesses will be able to conduct important face-to-face meetings or hold workplace events that are important for networking or team-bonding.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Businesses can do several things to prepare for reopening.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, encourage and facilitate all medically-eligible employees, especially those involved in high-touch point activities, to get vaccinated and deploy those who cannot be vaccinated to lower-risk settings.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second, integrate the use of ART self-tests into your work processes, especially for businesses that provide high touchpoint services or which tap on a pool of workers that frequently change.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Encourage employees to self-isolate and get themselves tested if they are not feeling well or if they suspect they may have been exposed to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Doing so can help detect cases early and limit the extent of disruption to your business.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I know of several employers who have made bulk purchases of testing kits, so their staff can easily access them if needed.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is a good idea and I encourage more employers to do the same.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As a small and open economy, we simply do not have the luxury of closing ourselves off to the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many parts of our economy require a steady flow of people in and out of Singapore, be it workers or visitors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As a business hub, many of our executives have to travel to manage and grow their regional businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our tourism and MICE industry, as well as our air hub status, also critically depend on international connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We should also not forget the international community based here.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many have not been able to return home to visit their families since the start of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is because if they go home, they may not be able to return to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There are also Singaporeans whose loved ones are stranded overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is a critical move that will allow us to reassert Singapore's position as a business, travel and talent hub.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This means that domestically, infected cases will create much less disruption than they do today and our businesses can largely return to normal operations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For the majority of cases, businesses will not have to shut down their premises for deep cleaning and we need not commit huge resources towards contact tracing.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Instead, infected individuals with mild symptoms may be able to recover from home and close contacts will likely just be required to monitor their health without the need for quarantine or self-isolation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is similar to how we treat influenza cases today.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Globally, Singapore will likely be one of the highest vaccinated countries in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will be able to regain strong air and maritime connectivity to a large number of countries, while ensuring that our healthcare system is well-functioning and not over-stretched by COVID-19 cases.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will make us one of the best places to work and live in the region and across the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Businesses have in fact continued to show confidence in our strong fundamentals during the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will continue to work hard to pursue projects that help companies grow and create good jobs and meaningful careers for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Before I end, I would like to thank Singaporeans, our businesses and our workers for walking this journey with us for the last 18 months.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It has been tremendously difficult for many of you and we are deeply appreciative of the commitment and grit that you have shown.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are so close to reaching the end of the tunnel.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will soon achieve a high vaccination coverage which will allow us to move decisively to a COVID-19-resilient state.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I want to appeal to everyone to not lose heart and work together to press on in our journey.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The latest outbreak is a major setback for all of us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many have been surprised at the size of these new clusters.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It shows how easy it is for the Delta variant to spread and cause large outbreaks with the potential to overwhelm our hospital system.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Furthermore, in a mixed population of vaccinated and unvaccinated persons, we are more likely to see large clusters because vaccinated persons can be infected but experience very mild symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Consequently, they may not realise they are infected and inadvertently, become asymptomatic carriers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: By the time the cases pop up, days or even weeks would have passed and the infection would have spread to many people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because of these large clusters, we faced a heightened risk of widespread community transmission before we attained adequate vaccine protection.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must remember that the proportion of people with two doses and with two weeks after their second shot was still less than 50%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will help to slow down transmission in the community and crucially, this will give us time to push up vaccination rates further and protect our seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I know the restrictions have caused much inconvenience to everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope our explanations will help you understand why we had to reintroduce these painful but necessary measures to protect our seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will elaborate on this in my Statement later this afternoon on the Supplementary Supply Bill and we hope the support measures will help affected workers and businesses tide over the Heightened Alert period.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we bring the current outbreak under control and continue to speed up vaccinations, we will be able to get our reopening plans back on track.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The key is to open up at the correct juncture.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some countries have decided to open up fully, even though their vaccination rates are less than ideal.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, the Netherlands lifted all restrictions when 45% of its population was fully vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Cases surged ten-fold to an average of 10,000 a day within two weeks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The UK has about 55% of its population fully vaccinated, although its coverage of its seniors is much higher at above 90%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It lifted all restrictions on 19 July, its "Freedom Day".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Cases have surged to 50,000 a day, more than two-thirds of its peak in the last wave and are likely to rise further.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Hospitalisation and death rates are starting to creep up again, almost entirely amongst unvaccinated individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are watching what is happening in these countries very closely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What is clear to the Multi-Ministry Taskforce (MTF) and our medical advisors is that we should be very careful about lifting restrictions when a significant proportion of our people are still not fully vaccinated, especially our more vulnerable seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While other countries may have come to terms with a certain level of COVID-19 cases and even deaths, this is not the choice we want to make in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Here, we look out for one another and we take care of each other.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do not want to see large numbers of COVID-19 patients in intensive care, on oxygen supplementation, let alone succumbing to the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we must give our fellow Singaporeans more time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, many younger Singaporeans are still waiting for their second dose of the vaccine.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And many of our seniors who had been hesitant about getting vaccinated are now starting to step forward.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will see continued improvements in our vaccination rates.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, there is no need to wait for everyone to be vaccinated before we begin to open up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That would mean holding back the entire re-opening timeline until much later in the year, which is not tenable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will synchronise our reopening with our vaccination coverage, not just of the overall population, but also amongst our seniors, who are the most vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we will do so in a series of controlled steps.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this is what we can all expect in the weeks ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In early August, at the midpoint of the Phase Two (Heightened Alert) period, we plan to review the current set of measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also monitor the status of the infected cases to confirm that the link between infection and hospitalisation has been weakened by the vaccines, like in the chart which Minister Ong showed just now.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This means that if you want to attend a large event or a religious service involving more than 100 persons, you have to be fully vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If you want to go out to dine in a restaurant or work out in a gym, you have to be fully vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We would then be able to ease the restrictions further, including allowing larger groups to get together, especially if they are fully vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We would also begin to reopen our borders, especially for vaccinated persons to travel.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will start by establishing travel corridors with countries or regions that have managed COVID-19 well and where the infection is similarly under control.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will allow vaccinated persons to travel more freely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those who are not vaccinated can still travel, but will be subject to the prevailing SHN requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond that, we will continue with a series of progressive easings.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we do, we must expect cases to rise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Partly because there is still ongoing cryptic transmission in our community, which can easily break out into new clusters with increased activity levels.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Also, as we open our borders for people to travel without SHN, we will see more imported cases and infected persons slipping through from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But at that stage, as you heard just now, our main focus would no longer be on daily case numbers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because the vast majority by then would have been vaccinated and even if they caught the virus, they would be much less likely to become very ill.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, our focus will be on the much smaller number of infected persons who need supplementary oxygen or require intensive care.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, at each stage of easing, we will monitor the health outcomes, especially the hospitalisation and ICU cases, closely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, we have to expect new variants to emerge, which may be more transmissible, more lethal, or more successful at evading the present vaccines.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will find solutions to these variants, especially through booster shots or updated vaccines, which we may need to roll out nationwide.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we must be prepared that the new variants can lead to more severe outbreaks and may well force us to introduce restrictions again from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In short, there are still considerable uncertainties about how the pandemic will unfold globally.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But our best bet is to push ahead with a high level of vaccine coverage for our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will give us the best chance to resume more normal lives, while keeping our morbidity and mortality rates low.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have provided an overview of the roadmap for our transition to a COVID-19-resilient society, where we learn to live with COVID-19 as part of our daily lives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The MTF is still fleshing out the details and we will share more when ready.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I assure everyone that we are committed to seeing through these plans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The current Heightened Alert is a temporary, limited timeout.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If many among our seniors are not vaccinated, we will continue to worry about our hospitalisation and ICU cases, as well as fatalities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I make a special plea to all who remain unvaccinated or have not registered to be vaccinated, especially our parents and grandparents: please come forward.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if you cannot get out of the house, we will send a team to your homes for the vaccination.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As part of our controlled and phased reopening, Safe Management Measures (SMMs) will still remain relevant and important.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Basic SMMs like keeping a safe distance from others and wearing a mask can help reduce transmission effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we must stay disciplined and continue to maintain these practices, even as we transition towards the new normal.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we would probably not want to do away completely with our mask requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We may consider dispensing with masks when outdoors, but it would still make sense to wear them in an indoor enclosed environment where transmission risks are greater.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this may well be one of the last rules to go in the new normal.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we will continue with our regular enforcement checks and take strict actions against any breaches of the rules.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members have asked questions about this, especially how our nightlife establishments are monitored and I believe Minister Shanmugam will be sharing more on this later, especially efforts by MHA and the Police.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But let me just say that our enforcement agencies are doing everything they can, under very challenging circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since April last year, a multi-agency task force comprising various Government agencies, including the Police, have been coordinating the enforcement of Safe Management and Safe Distancing Measures in public venues, including F&B outlets and massage and spa establishments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Where laws were flouted, offenders, both operators and individuals, have been taken to task and cases publicised.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our Safe Distancing Ambassadors and enforcement officers will continue to do their best and we should give them our full support.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most importantly, we must all do our part and continue to exercise individual and social responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We cannot rely on enforcement efforts alone to get us through this pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our society will be much safer if we demonstrate social solidarity and a collective sense of responsibility to do the right things together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are a few simple but very effective precautions which we should all incorporate into our daily routines.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have said probably like a million times but I think it is worth repeating.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Remember what I said earlier at the start that vaccinated persons can get infected and may feel very mild symptoms or even no symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, if you are feeling unwell – even vaccinated – feeling unwell with very mild symptoms, get yourself tested.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Antigen Rapid Test Kits – self-test kits – are widely available at all general retailers now.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If you buy in bulk, it is cheaper too.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, you can buy a few and have them at home.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, we have the breathalyser test in Parliament too before each Parliamentary session.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, regular testing and the social consciousness to get ourselves tested regularly, will protect us and keep us safe as we transit to the new normal.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But over the past year and a half, the vast majority of Singaporeans have shown tremendous discipline.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many have also been working tirelessly in our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not just our healthcare workers like our doctors and nurses at our hospitals, clinics and community care facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is also our fellow Singaporeans on the frontlines elsewhere, some in less expected settings, others in less visible places.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They include our Safe Distancing Ambassadors, food delivery riders, cleaners and many more.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They work hard to keep Singapore going and to keep all of us safe.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Like Mr Lok Chun Kiet, a cleaner with CBM Pte Ltd.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He attends to high-risk locations where positive cases have been detected.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The cleaning work that he does is not easy under normal circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But now, with the exposure to the virus, he and his team have to put on full personal protective equipment (PPE) and adhere closely to stringent procedures while they work.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is because of people like Chun Kiet and his team that we are able to quickly deep-clean our infected premises and minimise the risks of fomite transmissions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Or Ms Siti Zulaina Bte Md Said, a senior medical technologist with the National Public Health Laboratory at the NCID.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: She leads the team to investigate outbreaks and undertake testing surveillance.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is mission-critical work that requires long hours, stretching into weekends and public holidays.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You can imagine the load coming through recently with the surge of cases we have had in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is because of people like Siti and her team that we are able to detect and ringfence infections early.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are many more Chun Kiets and Sitis out there.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many more unsung heroes and heroines quietly and steadfastly contributing to our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am sure the entire House will join me in saying to all of them a big heartfelt "Thank You".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are all disappointed by the latest outbreak and the Heightened Alert restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, let us be strong and keep the faith.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us approach it with renewed strength as one people.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For example, I can refer to a Facebook post by Mr Alan John, former editor of The Straits Times, raising some of these questions in a very succinct way and making a number of fair points based on his understanding of the facts.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: First, why were KTVs allowed to change into F&B operations?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: During the circuit breaker last year, nightlife outlets were shut from 27 March 2020, together with many other businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: From Phase Two in June 2020, many businesses were allowed to reopen, including dine-in at F&B outlets.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Massage establishments were also allowed to open with conditions but KTVs were not allowed to reopen.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We took a stricter approach with KTVs because singing was considered a high-risk activity in an indoor setting and has a higher risk of transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In August 2020, the Singapore Nightlife Business Association (SNBA), the Singapore Entertainment Affiliation (SEA), other associations as well as individual businesses appealed for KTVs to re-open.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They had been closed by then for several months.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Jobs, the livelihoods of those in the KTV industries, the workers and their jobs were at risk and badly affected even with financial support from the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Some of us met directly with the KTV businesses in August 2020 and listened to them.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They asked to have singing and dancing to resume and they proposed a pilot with a maximum of five persons in a room.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Masks would be worn when not singing and disposable microphone covers would be used and they referred to other countries, including South Korea, where this had been allowed.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Others proposed changing their business models to F&B outlets.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They needed help to get new permits, change their use for F&B and so on; and for many, the situation was desperate.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We considered their suggestions and weighed the risks.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is illegal to have any kind of KTV operations.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Then, to the group that had asked to move over to provide F&B on a temporary basis, we said okay to that; again, with several conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Because basically, anyone can offer and open an F&B outlet.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Government cannot specifically say no to KTV outlets which want to become F&B outlets, provided they have the space to be an F&B outlet, the premises allow F&B outlets and they can get the approval from Singapore Food Agency (SFA), the land-use permissions and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The pivoted businesses would need a food preparation area to prepare and serve food, adequate indoor dining area for customers to be seated, to have their meals and with safe distancing in place.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Once converted to F&B, they were subject to the same safe management measures (SMMs) imposed on F&B outlets, meaning no inter-mingling amongst patrons and staff, no live music, no performances and various other conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, in summary, from March 2020: one, KTVs were not to operate; and two, some KTVs were allowed to become F&B outlets; as well as some pubs and bars, as they were also allowed to pivot to F&B outlets.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, as of March of this year, after several months of operations of these massage establishments, former pubs, bars and KTV businesses pivoting to being F&B outlets and so on, the situation was stable and the number of infections was generally low.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, that is the context and the background to why pubs, bars and KTV outlets were allowed to pivot and provide F&B.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There have been suggestions ranging from: we were in effect in cahoots with KTVs, which is a suggestion in a recent and quite unbalanced Nikkei article; or alternatively, we were very naive to not realise what happens at KTVs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The truth – we were neither in cahoots with the KTV operators nor are we as naive as some suggested.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think most people will accept it will be wrong to treat all the 430-odd businesses – KTV operators, pubs and bars – who want to change to provide F&B automatically as crooks.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They want to pivot over to provide F&B, that is the only way they can survive.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If you ask SNBA and SEA, there are KTVs which cater to families, there are many which do legitimate business and they were crying out for help.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Should we have said to them, "No, you cannot convert to F&B"?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For some, if you look at their premises, darkened rooms, not the most optimal for dining and people might well say, "Why would I want to go here for dining?" It appears common sensical to say this is dodgy and doubtful.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But in law, it is not so straightforward.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If a person comes to you and says, "Yes, I want to convert and I will keep to the rules.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: My business was perfectly legal in the past and now, I will continue to be legal." Then, the agencies will have to look him in the eye and say, "You cannot get a licence to become a food place because we do not think you are going to keep to the law in future.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We think you are going to break the law, even though you have committed no offence and even though you confirm that you will follow the rules." I will come back to this later.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, in addition to seeing if we can say no to those with dodgy reputations, part of the answer has got to be enforcement.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I will also say, realistically, the people who are going to cheat, going to do illegal things, will do them anyway.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They will use lounges, flats, warehouses, various places.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It has gone on and I am sure it goes on, regardless of whether we allow the change to F&B.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And there have been several illegal operations in different places outside of KTV outlets or ex-KTV outlets which have been busted.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As of November 2020, it was a risk-assessed approach and in general, it was working if you look at it as of March this year with a relatively low number of cases.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We then had the Delta variant, completely different transmissibility.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That variant came into the KTVs and created a cluster.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Minister for Health, my colleague, has spoken about it a number of times to clarify it.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The confusion is that the KTV cluster was somehow the reason for the recent Phase Two (Heightened Alert) tightened restrictions imposed on 22 July, but that is not so.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If we had only the KTV cluster, then we would not have had to move to Phase Two (Heightened Alert) or the tightened restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In fact, the MTF, as the Minister pointed out, considered the KTV cluster and decided we can manage it without having to impose any additional restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, let me summarise by making three points.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: About 430 businesses pivoted to F&B for several months.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Cases of infections overall in Singapore were low.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The new Delta variant caused a KTV cluster that has been brought under control.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And finally, if we were facing only the KTV cluster, there would have been no need for any tightened measures.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It has spread from the ports to the markets and the hawkers and into the wider community.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Some are under the misimpression that the virus went from the KTVs to the fishery port.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The evidence that we have does not suggest that.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The virus seems to have come from the region to our port, JFP.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: With this background, there is a live issue which I will share with Members.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The SNBA has sent an open letter, appealed for the industry to work more closely with the Government to report illegal activities, among other things, and they have also pointed out pivoting has helped many legitimate businesses to survive.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, should we allow them to reopen and continue as F&B operations?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This brings me to the earlier question I posed.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Some of them, when you look at the premises, you do question if they can really be F&B, but it requires us to say, flat out, to the operators, "Regardless of what you say, I am not going to believe you and I am not going to allow you to operate as an F&B".

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
